en: Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator for premature babies in rural areas without electricity.
The Sampaguita, the Philippine national flower, releases its strongest fragrance at night to attract pollinating moths.
The Ifugao built the Banaue Rice Terraces using an ancient stone-walling technique that prevents soil erosion on steep mountains.
The Philippine carabao, the national animal, has a sparse hair coat and sweat glands that help it survive hot tropical climates.
The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo injected millions of tons of sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere, temporarily cooling global temperatures.
Horticulturist Ramon Barba discovered how to induce mango trees to flower year-round using a simple potassium nitrate salt solution.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, has a unique crest of dark feathers and hunts monkeys and flying lemurs in forests.
The Department of Health scientifically validated the antibacterial properties of oregano leaves, making it an approved herbal cough medicine.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea contains over 600 species of fish and 360 species of coral.
Abaca, a Philippine native banana plant, produces the world's strongest natural fiber, which is used to make durable Manila ropes.
Jose Rizal, the national hero, studied astronomy and used a telescope to observe the stars and planets while exiled in Dapitan.
The Philippine pearl, the national gem, is produced by the gold-lip pearl oyster found in the coastal waters of Palawan.
